    // The de-homogenized control point of a NURBS curve.
    WeightedControlPoint(self: NurbsCurve3D, index: Integer): Vector3D
        => self.ControlPoints[index].PositionVector * self.Weights[index];

    //==
    // # Cox-de Boor basis functions

    // A ratio that reads as zero when its denominator vanishes. Every repeated
    // knot produces a 0/0 in the recurrence, and the convention that those terms
    // are zero is what makes repeated knots mean "reduced continuity" rather than
    // "undefined".
    KnotRatio(numerator: Number, denominator: Number): Number
        => denominator == 0.0 ? 0.0 : numerator / denominator;

    // The zero-degree basis: one on the half-open span [k_i, k_i+1), zero
    // elsewhere. The final span is closed on the right instead, so that the
    // curve is defined AT the end of its domain rather than collapsing to the
    // origin there — the usual special case, expressed by passing the domain end
    // down rather than by clamping the parameter short of it.
    ZeroDegreeBasis(knots: KnotVector, domainEnd: Number, i: Integer, t: Number): Number
        => knots.KnotAt(i) <= t
           && (t < knots.KnotAt(i + 1)
               || t >= domainEnd && knots.KnotAt(i) < domainEnd && knots.KnotAt(i + 1) >= domainEnd)
            ? 1.0
            : 0.0;

    // The i-th B-spline basis function of the given degree at parameter t.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-spline#Definition
    BasisFunction(knots: KnotVector, domainEnd: Number, i: Integer, degree: Integer, t: Number): Number
        => degree <= 0
            ? ZeroDegreeBasis(knots, domainEnd, i, t)
            : KnotRatio(t - knots.KnotAt(i), knots.KnotAt(i + degree) - knots.KnotAt(i))
                  * BasisFunction(knots, domainEnd, i, degree - 1, t)
            + KnotRatio(knots.KnotAt(i + degree + 1) - t,
                        knots.KnotAt(i + degree + 1) - knots.KnotAt(i + 1))
                  * BasisFunction(knots, domainEnd, i + 1, degree - 1, t);

    //==
    // # ICurve evaluation
    //
    // `Eval` takes the unit parameter every ICurve2D / ICurve3D takes, so it is
    // mapped onto the curve's own knot domain first. Values outside [0, 1] clamp
    // to the ends rather than extrapolating: outside the domain the basis is not
    // a partition of unity and the "extrapolated" point is meaningless.

    // The knot parameter a unit curve parameter names.
    KnotParameter(domain: NumberInterval, t: Number): Number
        => domain.Lerp(t.Clamp(0.0, 1.0));

    // The point at the given unit parameter: the basis-weighted sum of the
    // control points.
    Eval(self: BSplineCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D {
        var domain = self.ParameterDomain;
        var u = KnotParameter(domain, t);
        var sum = self.ControlPoints.Count.Range.Reduce(Vector2D.Zero, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.ControlPoints[i].PositionVector
                * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        return (sum.X, sum.Y);
    }

    // The point at the given unit parameter.
    Eval(self: BSplineCurve3D, t: Number): Point3D {
        var domain = self.ParameterDomain;
        var u = KnotParameter(domain, t);
        var sum = self.ControlPoints.Count.Range.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.ControlPoints[i].PositionVector
                * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        return (sum.X, sum.Y, sum.Z);
    }

    // The point at the given unit parameter: the weighted basis sum divided by
    // the summed weights, which is the projection back out of homogeneous space
    // that makes a NURBS curve rational — and lets it represent conics exactly.
    Eval(self: NurbsCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D {
        var domain = self.ParameterDomain;
        var u = KnotParameter(domain, t);
        var count = self.ControlPoints.Count;
        var numerator = count.Range.Reduce(Vector2D.Zero, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.WeightedControlPoint(i)
                * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        var denominator = count.Range.Reduce(0.0, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.Weights[i] * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        var p = denominator == 0.0 ? numerator : numerator / denominator;
        return (p.X, p.Y);
    }

    // The point at the given unit parameter.
    Eval(self: NurbsCurve3D, t: Number): Point3D {
        var domain = self.ParameterDomain;
        var u = KnotParameter(domain, t);
        var count = self.ControlPoints.Count;
        var numerator = count.Range.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.WeightedControlPoint(i)
                * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        var denominator = count.Range.Reduce(0.0, (acc, i) =>
            acc + self.Weights[i] * BasisFunction(self.Knots, domain.End, i, self.Degree, u));
        var p = denominator == 0.0 ? numerator : numerator / denominator;
        return (p.X, p.Y, p.Z);
    }

    //==
    // # Piecewise indexing and Hermite evaluation
    //
    // Evaluation of the Hermite curves declared in `splines.types.plato`, plus the
    // piecewise indexing helpers every point-chain spline in the splines family is
    // built on: turning the canonical [0,1] curve parameter into a segment index
    // plus a local parameter, and reading the right control values out of the
    // parallel arrays. The cubic Hermite basis itself lives in
    // `library Polynomials` (`polynomials.types.plato`), generic over `INumerical`;
    // nothing is reimplemented here.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * A chain of n points has n - 1 spans when open and n when Closed (the
    //     last point joins back to the first).
    //   * Control points are converted to displacements with PositionVector before
    //     entering a `INumerical`-generic basis function and back with ToPoint, the
    //     explicit point/vector converters from `library Transforms`.

    //==
    // # Piecewise indexing helpers

    // The number of spans in a chain of `count` points: count - 1 when open,
    // count when closed. Precondition: count >= 2.
    SpanCount(count: Integer, closed: Boolean): Integer
        => closed ? count : count - 1;

    // The index of the span containing the canonical parameter t, clamped into
    // [0, SpanCount - 1] so that t = 1 lands on the last span rather than one
    // past it. Precondition: count >= 2.
    SpanIndex(count: Integer, closed: Boolean, t: Number): Integer
        => (t * count.SpanCount(closed).ToNumber).Floor.ToInteger
               .Clamp(0, count.SpanCount(closed) - 1);

    // The local parameter within the span that SpanIndex selects, in [0, 1].
    SpanFraction(count: Integer, closed: Boolean, t: Number): Number
        => t * count.SpanCount(closed).ToNumber
           - count.SpanIndex(closed, t).ToNumber;

    // Element i of a chain: taken modulo the count when the chain is closed and
    // clamped to the ends when it is open. The "+ count then modulo" corrects
    // the truncated remainder, which is negative for i = -1. Lets one body
    // serve open and closed chains and both end conditions.
    AtWrapped(xs: Array<$T>, i: Integer, closed: Boolean): $T
        => closed ? xs[((i % xs.Count) + xs.Count) % xs.Count]
                  : xs[i.Clamp(0, xs.Count - 1)];

    //==
    // # Hermite curves
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubic_Hermite_spline

    // The point on a single cubic Hermite segment at t.
    Eval(self: HermiteCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.Start.PositionVector
               .Hermite(self.End.PositionVector, self.StartTangent, self.EndTangent, t)
               .ToPoint;
